subject: Information Theory
title: Entropy Is Everywhere
description: A 60-second lesson on Entropy Is Everywhere.

hook.text: Linguistics, genetics, finance, neuroscience, ecology. Shannon's formula shows up in every field. Why?

buildup.text: Entropy is a property of probability distributions. Every field that uses probabilities can use entropy.

discovery.text: It answers the universal question: how surprised should I be on average? That question is everywhere.

twist.text: Some fields rediscovered entropy independently before learning Shannon had formalized it decades earlier.

climax.text: Entropy is the rare formula that transcends domain. It connects physics, biology, AI, and human thought.

punchline.text: One formula. Every field. Average surprise.

quiz.question: Why does Shannon's entropy appear across so many fields?
options: It measures a universal property of probability distributions
It's the only formula involving logarithms
